🇳🇵 Nepal–Tibet Border Avalanche & Flood | 26 August 2026 A major ice–rock avalanche near the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a cascading hazard: a large glacier mass collapsed from high elevation, sending ice, rock and sediment into the Lhende Khola. The debris blocked the river and formed a temporary barrier lake, which then released a powerful downstream surge of muddy water, debris and boulders. 🌡️ Possible factors: glacier instability, melting ice, steep crevassed terrain, meltwater lubrication and possible seismic triggering. ⚠️ Some claims remain unconfirmed, so the exact trigger requires scientific investigation. 🌊 Avalanche → Debris Flow → River Blockage → Dam Breach → Flood #Nepal #NepalFlood #NepalLandslide #NepalAvalanche #NepalTibetBorder Himalayas HimalayanAvalanche Landslide GlacierCollapse GlacialLake BarrierLake FlashFlood DebrisFlow LhendeKhola Bhotekoshi ClimateChange GlacierMelt NaturalDisaster DisasterScience EarthScience 26August2026

The flooding damaged the structures and transmission line towers of the 40 MW Rahughat Hydropower Project in the Myagdi district, a facility recently integrated into Nepal's power grid. #nepal #myagdi #floods #brekingnews  27 сентября 2026 года Мьягди, Непал Наводнения и оползни, вызванные непрекращающимися дождями, нарушили работу энергосетей, что привело к остановке генерации более 900 мегаватт электроэнергии по всей стране. Паводки повредили сооружения и опоры линий электропередачи Гидроэнергетического проекта Рахугат мощностью 40 МВт в районе Мьягди, объект, недавно интегрированный в энергосистему Непала.

Journalist Bidhya Chapagain broke down in tears after witnessing the difficult living conditions of people in Ripa village of Humla, Karnali. But with the bridge still unbuilt, locals continue to depend on a tuin to cross the river. Despite changes in governments over the years, the community is still waiting for basic connectivity. Edit: I want to add one thing to what I said. After sitting with everything and watching the video back several times, I can understand why the way I delivered that message was hurtful, especially to people directly affected by what happened in Nepal. I genuinely am sorry for that. I wasn’t laughing at anyone’s suffering or celebrating anyone’s death, and that was never my heart.
